summary: Stone three-story Forest Service lookout on Terry Peak near Lead, SD; manned from 1950, cab removed, stone base open to visitors; NHLR-registered 2026.

facts.design: three-story stone structure with a 10-foot stone base
facts.status_note: The cab has been removed but the base remains; the stone base has an open observation platform.

access.note: Forest Service viewing area for tourists; a Black Hills hiking site says the tower is open to the public

events.note: NHLR gives 1949-1950 and firelookout.com gives 1950; construction of the stone understructure was under way in 1949
Near completion and ready to be manned by late August 1950; Vernon Tollefson due on duty September 1
Lightning hit the lookout and area, knocking out radios and telephones; partial power restored that night
Fire room raised on stilts and a visitor room built between it and the quarters, after the Forest Service separated visitors from fire work
More than 65,000 people visited the tower in 1962, per a 1963 newspaper
NHLR: out of service as a fire lookout by 1973
firelookout.com: enclosed visitor deck and upper cab removed in 1978; a 2011 history book says the top two levels were removed in the 1970s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says 1949-1950 and firelookout.com says 1950. A 1949 newspaper shows construction starting that year and a 1950 newspaper shows it manned in August 1950. The story uses 1950 for completion and mentions 1949 as the start.

NHLR says the lookout was out of service by 1973; firelookout.com dates removal of the visitor deck and cab to 1978; a 2011 history book (Images of America: Black Hills National Forest) says the top two levels were removed in the 1970s. The story gives the range rather than choosing one date.
NHLR gives 7,066 ft (2,154 m); firelookout.com gives 7064 ft. Elevation is not a fact key here, so the difference is noted only.

notes_for_editor: Strong record: NHLR, firelookout.com, a long newspaper transcript page and the FFLA list agree on the core story. Open points: the removal year of the upper floors (1973 vs 1978 vs 1970s) and the 1949 vs 1950 build year are reported as ranges. The 1978 removal date and the 1970s date in the 2011 book are from the sources as printed. The travel-site wording about the road is a blog claim, so the story keeps it as a note. The record's height_m 4.3 is unsupported and is proposed for removal. The 1950s-1960s named lookouts are from firelookout.com and the newspaper; names are historical, not verified against Forest Service records.
